concepts.title: Meaning of Environment and Environmental Concerns

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaning of Environment and Environmental Concerns' refers to.
questions.a: The environment refers to the natural world -- land, water, air, forests and biodiversity -- that sustains life, and environmental concerns in global politics arise from the degradation of these resources through pollution, deforestation and over-exploitation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning of Environment and Environmental Concerns'.
questions.a: Environmental concerns have entered global politics because the degradation of nature -- pollution, deforestation, resource depletion -- threatens the survival and well-being of people across national borders.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Meaning of Environment and Environmental Concerns' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Introduction: Environmental Concerns in Global Politics

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Protection of the Global Commons' refers to.
questions.a: The global commons are natural resources and areas that lie outside the jurisdiction of any one state -- such as the earth's atmosphere, Antarctica, the high seas and outer space -- and require collective international cooperation for their protection.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Protection of the Global Commons'.
questions.a: The global commons are shared resources not owned by any single state; their protection requires international agreements because no one state can manage or protect them alone.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Protection of the Global Commons' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Protection of the Global Commons

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Common Property Resources' refers to.
questions.a: Common property resources are natural resources like forests, grazing lands, ponds and fisheries that are collectively owned and managed by local communities, distinct from both private property and the open-access global commons.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Common Property Resources'.
questions.a: Common property resources are community-owned resources governed by local rules and customs; they are neither private property nor global commons, and their sustainable management depends on community institutions.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Common Property Resources' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Common Property Resources

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Indigenous Peoples and the Environment' refers to.
questions.a: Indigenous peoples are native communities who have lived in close harmony with their natural environment for centuries, possessing traditional knowledge of sustainable resource use and facing threats to their lands and way of life from deforestation, mining and state development projects.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Indigenous Peoples and the Environment'.
questions.a: Indigenous peoples depend on and protect their natural environment through traditional knowledge; their displacement and loss of land due to development projects is a major environmental and human rights concern.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Indigenous Peoples and the Environment' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Indigenous Peoples and their Environment

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Environmental Movements' refers to.
questions.a: Environmental movements are collective campaigns by people and organisations to protect nature and natural resources from degradation, often arising when state policies and development projects threaten local livelihoods and ecosystems.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Environmental Movements'.
questions.a: Environmental movements are people's struggles to protect forests, rivers and land from destructive development, combining ecological concerns with the defence of local livelihoods and rights.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Environmental Movements' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Environmental Movements

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Environmental Movements in India' refers to.
questions.a: India has witnessed significant environmental movements such as the Chipko movement (tree-hugging to prevent deforestation), the Narmada Bachao Andolan (against large dams), and the Silent Valley movement (against a hydroelectric project in Kerala), which link ecological protection with people's livelihoods.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Environmental Movements in India'.
questions.a: India's environmental movements -- Chipko, Narmada Bachao Andolan and Silent Valley -- combine ecological concerns with the defence of local communities' livelihoods and rights against destructive development projects.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Environmental Movements in India' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Environmental Movements in India

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Wildlife Conservation' refers to.
questions.a: Wildlife conservation is the protection and preservation of animal and plant species and their habitats from extinction and degradation, achieved through national parks, sanctuaries, legislation and international conventions like CITES.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Wildlife Conservation'.
questions.a: Wildlife conservation protects biodiversity from extinction caused by habitat loss, poaching and pollution, using protected areas, laws like the Wildlife Protection Act and international agreements such as CITES.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Wildlife Conservation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Wildlife Conservation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sustainable Development' refers to.
questions.a: Sustainable development is development that meets the needs of the present generation without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs, as defined by the Brundtland Commission in 1987, balancing economic growth with environmental protection.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sustainable Development'.
questions.a: Sustainable development balances economic growth, social justice and environmental protection so that present needs are met without harming the ability of future generations to meet theirs.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Sustainable Development' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Sustainable Development

concepts.title: Environmental Concerns in Global Politics: The North-South Divide

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Environmental Concerns in Global Politics: The North-South Divide' refers to.
questions.a: The North-South divide in environmental politics refers to the disagreement between developed (Northern) and developing (Southern) countries over responsibility for environmental degradation, with the South arguing that the North's historical consumption caused the crisis and should bear greater responsibility.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Environmental Concerns in Global Politics: The North-South Divide'.
questions.a: The North-South divide highlights that developed countries are historically responsible for most environmental damage, while developing countries argue for the right to develop and demand that the North bear greater responsibility and costs.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Environmental Concerns in Global Politics: The North-South Divide' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Environmental Concerns: North-South Divide
